meta.note: Los hechos provienen de los artículos originales enlazados. La IA solo traduce y resume; no genera noticias.

es.title: Noticias de Copyright e Inteligencia Artificial
es.subtitle: Notas publicadas por medios reales de la industria, con liga al artículo original. Sin noticias inventadas.

items.title: “A Cute Little LibGen Babysitter”: Music Publishers Sue Anthropic Founders Over Torrenting Spree
items.summary: Los principales editores musicales, entre ellos Sony Music y Warner Chappell, demandan a Anthropic y a sus fundadores por descargar masivamente libros piratas de LibGen y Pirate Library Mirror, alegando que la misma actividad también infringió obras musicales y que se vinculó a un acuerdo de 1,5 mil millones de dólares.

items.title: SOCAN sues Suno over AI music copyright infringement
items.summary: SOCAN ha presentado una demanda contra Suno, alegando que la plataforma de generación musical basada en IA infringe derechos de autor al utilizar obras musicales sin la autorización correspondiente.

items.title: Latest Suno lawsuit accuses AI company of violating the publicity rights of musicians rather than infringing their copyrights
items.summary: Un grupo de músicos acusa a Suno de violar sus derechos de publicidad en EE. UU. al codificar sus identidades en el modelo de IA y luego explotar públicamente sus nombres, sin referirse a una infracción de derechos de autor.

items.title: The Sony and Warner music publishers finally get round to suing Anthropic
items.summary: Las editoriales Sony y Warner han presentado una demanda contra la empresa de IA Anthropic y sus fundadores, Ben Mann y Dario Amodei, alegando su participación directa en la descarga ilegal de partituras y letras piratas.

items.title: Donald Trump’s DoJ says OpenAI should be able to do whatever it wants with copyright protected works
items.summary: El Departamento de Justicia de EE. UU. intervino en la disputa entre The New York Times y OpenAI, argumentando que el entrenamiento de IA constituye un uso justo bajo la ley de derechos de autor, un punto central en múltiples litigios del sector musical.

items.title: Adult Film Producer Unmasks Prolific ‘John Doe’ Torrent Pirate as Meta Executive
items.summary: Un productor de cine adulto vincula una demanda contra un “John Doe” con el caso de entrenamiento de IA contra Meta, alegando que un ejecutivo de Reality Labs descargó cerca de 20 000 archivos en su casa para trabajo, mientras Meta niega la conexión con la empresa.

items.title: YouTube Terms of Service Allow AI Music Training, Google Says in Copyright Lawsuit
items.summary: Google argumenta en una demanda de derechos de autor que los Términos de Servicio de YouTube autorizan el uso de su contenido para entrenar sistemas de IA musical, defendiendo la legalidad de dicha práctica.

items.title: Suno and Believe Music Announce Strategic Partnership
items.summary: Suno, la plataforma de generación musical por IA, anunció una asociación estratégica con Believe Music, ampliando sus acuerdos de licencia previamente firmados con Warner Music y BMG, y extendiendo la colaboración a TuneCore.

items.title: Jason Isbell’s Suno lawsuit takes aim beyond AI copyright
items.summary: La demanda presentada por Jason Isbell contra Suno se enfoca en cuestiones que van más allá de la infracción de derechos de autor por IA, abordando aspectos adicionales de la relación entre artistas y tecnología.

items.title: Stray Kids Label Hits Music Distributor With DMCA Subpoena Over Bootleg Track
items.summary: JYP Entertainment, sello de Stray Kids, emitió una citación DMCA al distribuidor Symphonic para obtener nombres, direcciones IP y datos bancarios del responsable de distribuir una pista bootleg del grupo en Apple Music y TikTok.

items.title: Suno Licensing Deals Raise New Issue in AI Copyright Fight With Universal, Sony
items.summary: Los acuerdos de licencia de Suno con grandes discográficas generan un nuevo punto de discusión en la disputa de derechos de autor de IA contra Universal y Sony, al introducir consideraciones sobre el alcance de dichas licencias.

items.title: Suno admits it obtained YouTube audio to train its AI – but challenges UMG and Sony’s standing to bring ‘stream ripping’ claim
items.summary: Suno confirmó que utilizó audio de YouTube para entrenar su IA musical y, al mismo tiempo, cuestionó la legitimidad de las demandas de UMG y Sony que acusan a la empresa de “stream ripping” para entrenar sus modelos.

tip.title: Antes de firmar, revisa la reversión de derechos
tip.body: La pregunta clave de cualquier contrato no es cuánto te dan hoy, sino cuándo y cómo recuperas tu obra. Si no hay cláusula de reversión, estás cediendo por el plazo completo.

en.title: Copyright & Artificial Intelligence News
en.subtitle: Stories published by real industry outlets, each linked to its original article. No invented news.

items.title: “A Cute Little LibGen Babysitter”: Music Publishers Sue Anthropic Founders Over Torrenting Spree
items.summary: Major music publishers, including Sony Music and Warner Chappell, have filed lawsuits against Anthropic and its founders for bulk torrenting of pirated books from LibGen and Pirate Library Mirror, claiming the activity also infringed musical works and is tied to a $1.5 billion settlement.

items.title: SOCAN sues Suno over AI music copyright infringement
items.summary: SOCAN has filed a lawsuit against Suno, claiming that the AI‑driven music generation platform infringes copyright by using musical works without proper authorization.

items.title: Latest Suno lawsuit accuses AI company of violating the publicity rights of musicians rather than infringing their copyrights
items.summary: A coalition of musicians alleges that Suno breached U.S. publicity rights by encoding their identities into its AI model and publicly using their names, rather than asserting a traditional copyright infringement claim.

items.title: The Sony and Warner music publishers finally get round to suing Anthropic
items.summary: Sony and Warner music publishing companies have sued AI firm Anthropic and its founders, Ben Mann and Dario Amodei, alleging they were personally involved in the illegal downloading of pirated sheet music and lyrics.

items.title: Donald Trump’s DoJ says OpenAI should be able to do whatever it wants with copyright protected works
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice intervened in the New York Times vs. OpenAI case, asserting that AI training qualifies as fair use under copyright law, a key issue in numerous music‑industry lawsuits.

items.title: Adult Film Producer Unmasks Prolific ‘John Doe’ Torrent Pirate as Meta Executive
items.summary: An adult film producer connects a John Doe lawsuit to Meta’s AI‑training case, claiming a Reality Labs executive downloaded roughly 20,000 files at home for work purposes, while Meta disputes any link to the company.

items.title: YouTube Terms of Service Allow AI Music Training, Google Says in Copyright Lawsuit
items.summary: Google contends in a copyright lawsuit that YouTube’s Terms of Service permit the use of its audio for training AI music models, asserting that such training is permissible under the platform’s agreements.

items.title: Suno and Believe Music Announce Strategic Partnership
items.summary: Suno, the AI music generation platform, announced a strategic partnership with Believe Music, building on prior licensing deals with Warner Music and BMG and extending collaboration to include TuneCore.

items.title: Jason Isbell’s Suno lawsuit takes aim beyond AI copyright
items.summary: Jason Isbell’s lawsuit against Suno targets issues extending beyond AI copyright infringement, addressing broader concerns about the interaction between artists and the technology.

items.title: Stray Kids Label Hits Music Distributor With DMCA Subpoena Over Bootleg Track
items.summary: JYP Entertainment, Stray Kids’ label, served a DMCA subpoena to distributor Symphonic, seeking the offender’s name, IP address, and bank details after a solo track appeared as a bootleg on Apple Music and TikTok.

items.title: Suno Licensing Deals Raise New Issue in AI Copyright Fight With Universal, Sony
items.summary: Suno’s licensing agreements with major record labels introduce a new issue in the AI copyright battle with Universal and Sony, raising questions about the scope and impact of those licenses.

items.title: Suno admits it obtained YouTube audio to train its AI – but challenges UMG and Sony’s standing to bring ‘stream ripping’ claim
items.summary: Suno acknowledged using YouTube audio to train its AI and simultaneously challenged the standing of UMG and Sony’s lawsuits alleging “stream ripping” as the basis for their claims.

tip.title: Before signing, check the reversion clause
tip.body: The key question in any deal isn't what you get today —it's when and how you get your work back. With no reversion clause, you're assigning for the full term.
